name: Captivating Vampire
oracle_text:
Other Vampire creatures you control get +1/+1.
Tap five untapped Vampires you control: Gain control of target creature. It becomes a Vampire in addition to its other types.
blocked_sentences: Tap five untapped Vampires you control: Gain control of target creature. It becomes a Vampire in addition to its other types.

needs.what: an effect that moves a permanent's controller to the ability's controller for as long as the source remains on the battlefield -- it must retarget an object already on the battlefield rather than move it between zones, take the creature under the new controller's turn/attack timing, and hand control back if the source leaves
needs.why_existing_wont_do: No op in `ops` changes controller. The nearest reaches are `put_onto_battlefield`, which only brings an object in from another zone and so cannot touch a creature already in play, and `lock_abilities` / `must_attack` / `freeze`, which constrain an opponent's creature while leaving it theirs. `static_effects` likewise has no controller-changing entry -- `set_types`, `set_pt` and `buff` all rewrite characteristics, never controller.

needs.what: an activated-ability cost that taps N untapped permanents the player controls matching a filter (here: five untapped Vampires, the source itself eligible among them), chosen by the activating player at activation time and tapped as a cost rather than as an effect
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Cost supports tapping the source itself ({T}) but has no form that taps other permanents, and no way to require a count or a subtype filter on what is tapped. The `tap` op is an effect, not a cost: paying it as an effect would let the ability be activated with no untapped Vampires available and would put the taps on resolution instead of on activation.

needs.what: a one-shot effect that adds a creature type to a target permanent in addition to its existing types, for as long as the granting source stays on the battlefield
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `add_subtype` exists only in `static_effects`, where it applies continuously to a filtered set read off printed characteristics -- it cannot name the one creature an activated ability targeted. Among the ops, `animate` and `choose_type` set a body or pick a type wholesale rather than appending a subtype to an existing permanent, and `set_types` (a static effect) replaces the type line instead of adding to it.
